text: Maya: quick drop-in — kernel/cache update: Maya: what I did: ran small canary on kernel v2.3 with batching tweaks, exercised KV warmup path, collected perf traces. Maya: blocker: noticed repeated 99th spikes when a hot-shard misses the prefix cache during microbursts. need ideas on mitigation. Liam: nice work — do you have the trace ids? can we repro with the local qemu harness? Maya: trace ids attached in the perf dashboard link: https://perf.redwood/p/trace/8f3a — repros on `local-harness:1001` with synthetic burst. Sasha: I saw similar in yesterday's nightly — culprit looked like a KV eviction cascade when load crosses ~420 rps for 512-token sequences. Oli: possible quick wins: 1) bump KV max-staleness to 30s for the canary fleet, 2) enforce small prefetch window for shards with high miss-rate. Maya: tried bumping max-staleness to 20s, helped tail but increased memory pressure on the canary GPUs. Janice: how much mem delta? Maya: roughly +1.8GB per shard on a 48GB instance, so we hit OOM margin on canary nodes. Liam: can we flip to a hybrid: keep staleness low but do aggressive local prefetch for top-5 prefixes? Sasha: that aligns with my notes — top-5 hot-prefix cache reduced misses by ~68% in sim. Maya: plan for today: open PR with config experiment (batch_timeout=8ms, prefetch_top_k=5), run 2-hour canary and gather lat/p99s. Maya: ping @Oli for review on the PR once I open it. Oli: on it — I can review after standup. quick glance locally passed unit tests. deploy-bot: canary job started: canary/kernel-v2.3/exp-2024-11-08 (job id c-8923) Janice: FYI ops: if mem stays high we should have a rollback plan; can we set an automatic fallback to v2.2? Maya: yes — rollout config includes automatic fallback if node OOM rate > 0.5% over 5m. Liam: small ask — add a smoke test that simulates a 250ms burst every 30s to the canary harness; will catch cascade earlier. Sasha: adding that to the test harness now, will push a tiny change. Maya: blocker: need one more perf metric in the dashboard — 'cache-miss-cascade-count' — @Janice could you add a short Grafana panel? Janice: yes, will add panel and notify once live. Oli: review note: in the PR please include the microbenchmark results and the exact kernel cmdline change. small snippet suggestion: ``` --batch_timeout_ms=8 --prefetch.k=5 ``` Maya: will include those and the perf tables. Liam: if the canary looks good, we can do a phased rollout to 10% and monitor for 3 hours. Maya: thanks — will update here after the 2-hour canary. deploy-bot: canary update: 45m in — p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 42ms, p99 currently 162ms (baseline p99 was 210ms). Sasha: solid improvement so far. Maya: quick note — tagging PR as wip until Oli signs off. Oli: review complete, left one minor comment on config parsing. will approve after fix. Maya: thanks — merging after CI passes and Janice adds dashboard metric. :thumbsup: Liam: heads-up to oncall — small chance of transient mem growth, but fallback is in place. Maya: last: if anyone sees weird canary alerts ping me directly. Janice: dashboard panel pushed. Maya: closing loop — 2-hour canary finished, p99 dropped ~22% vs baseline, no OOMs observed during run. starting phased rollout to 10%. deploy-bot: rollout to 10% started (r-1094). Sasha: congrats team. Liam: nice win :) Maya: thanks all — I'll post the PR link and perf summary in #eng-runtime-reports later today.
